The Japanese Sayagata 紗綾形 pattern is built from interlocking swastika-like motifs (manji 卍) connected by continuous, unbroken lines into a repeating lattice. Its name comes from saya, a type of silk twill on which the design was traditionally woven. Because the lines never break or end, the pattern symbolizes eternity, continuity, and good fortune, and it was historically used as a lining for kimono and as a background motif in formal textiles to convey lasting prosperity and an unbroken family lineage.
